clue.text: Audibly protested about eg John, Paul, or George (not Ringo) being amplified

indicators.note: one thing placed about another surrounds it, so one piece is wrapped round the other

blocks.note: a crowd that protests out loud jeers and hoots

blocks.clueFragment: eg John, Paul, or George (not Ringo)
blocks.note: John, Paul and George are all saints, abbreviated ST; there is no Saint Ringo

explanation.surface: Fans loudly protest as three of the Beatles, minus their drummer, are put through the speakers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beatles are a red herring: the three named share the title Saint, which the drummer does not, hence 'not Ringo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound that has been boosted has been made louder, the same as amplified.

clue.text: Philosopher that's brought home successfully

blocks.note: first meaning: Francis ..., the English philosopher of science
second meaning: from the idiom for earning a living or succeeding, bringing home the cured pork

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'bring home the bacon' means to succeed or to earn the household's keep.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the Elizabethan thinker is also the cured meat in the idiom about winning a living.

clue.text: Refer to part of bible in speech for embellishment

indicators.note: something said to be in a thing sits inside it, so the first pieces are enclosed by the last

blocks.note: to name something is to mention or refer to it
the New Testament, abbreviated NT
a formal speech

explanation.surface: A preacher quotes scripture in a sermon to dress it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In speech' sounds like a homophone signal, but it only means the other pieces go inside a word for a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamentation is decoration added to make something more elaborate, which is what embellishment means.

clue.text: At that point, it's repeatedly said to offer reassurance

definitions.text: it's repeatedly said to offer reassurance

blocks.note: first meaning: in that place, as opposed to here

blocks.clueFragment: it's repeatedly said to offer reassurance
blocks.note: second meaning: the word doubled up is what you say to comfort someone upset

explanation.walkthrough: The soothing phrase is the word said twice, which is why the clue says 'repeatedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in that place, and doubled it is the stock phrase used to console a crying child.

clue.text: Put out of office, editor upset over attitude

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: ED is the usual abbreviation for editor
a pose is a stance or attitude struck

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor is sacked after a staff revolt against their manner.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'over' means the first piece sits above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To depose a ruler or official is to remove them from their position of power.

clue.text: Noted diarist? Yes, frantically penning page after page

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as animals are shut in a pen
doing something frantically means wildly and in disorder, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
P is the abbreviation for page, given twice

explanation.surface: A famous diarist agrees and writes furiously, filling one page after another.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Pepys kept the best-known diary in English, covering London in the 1660s, including the Great Fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepys is famous above all for his diary, so he is the archetypal noted diarist.

clue.text: Pacify situation around area, with temperature lower

indicators.note: with simply attaches one piece to the next, here stacking two of them
a word placed around others surrounds them, so the outer word is split to hold them

blocks.note: a place is a position or situation
A is the abbreviation for area
T is the abbreviation for temperature, placed below the A in this down entry

explanation.surface: Someone calms a tense situation in the district as the heat dies down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' is not a verb about cooling; in a down clue it says the temperature letter goes beneath the area letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To placate someone is to soothe or appease them, which is what pacify means.

clue.text: Lack of purpose? Not so, when embraced by heads

indicators.note: something embraced by others is hugged between them, so it sits inside

blocks.note: a point and a ness are both headlands, coastal heads jutting into the sea
less means not so much, as in less heavy for not so heavy

explanation.surface: Someone claims life has no purpose, and is contradicted by the people in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads' looks like bosses, but it supplies two geographical words for a headland, one placed each side.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointlessness is the state of having no point or purpose, which is a lack of purpose.

clue.text: Small sailing boat, first of yachts, partly designed

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of the following word is used

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A description of a little sailing vessel leading a fleet of yachts, only half drawn up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sketchy is rough and incomplete, like a plan only partly worked out.

clue.text: Study at four in place of worship, deep in thought

indicators.note: something in a building sits inside it, so these letters go within the next word

blocks.note: to con is an old word for studying or learning by heart
taken as written
IV is four in Roman numerals
a temple is a building for worship

explanation.surface: Someone meditating quietly in a temple at four o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: To con is a crossword favourite for to study.
explanation.definitionFit: A contemplative person is thoughtful and meditative, absorbed in reflection, which is being deep in thought.

clue.text: Paginates old book of verses

blocks.note: first meaning: assigns a numeral to each page
second meaning: the fourth book of the Old Testament

explanation.walkthrough: The Old Testament book, like all biblical books, is divided into numbered verses, which is what 'of verses' adds.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb form means puts a numeral on each page, and it is also the title of an Old Testament book.

clue.text: Tacit reform for Upper House?

indicators.note: to reform something is to form it again, giving the letters a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Quiet changes are proposed to the second chamber of a parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upper House' looks like a legislative chamber such as the House of Lords; the question mark flags that it means the top room of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is the room right under the roof, the uppermost part of a house.

clue.text: Rewrite any incomplete clue? Madness

indicators.note: incomplete means missing its end, so the last letter is dropped
to rewrite is to put the letters down again in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then cut short

explanation.surface: A frustrated solver thinks rewriting a half-finished clue would be crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunacy is insanity or extreme foolishness, a straightforward synonym for madness.

clue.text: Subsequently a learner produces creative kind of thinking

definitions.note: the answer is the adjective that precedes 'thinking' in the phrase

blocks.note: later means afterwards, subsequently
taken as written
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student who comes up with an inventive approach after a while.
explanation.walkthrough: Lateral thinking, a phrase coined by Edward de Bono, means solving problems by indirect, imaginative approaches.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral thinking is the term for creative, sideways problem-solving rather than step-by-step logic.

clue.text: Leader of Indians having powwow around tree

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front
a word placed around a letter surrounds it, so that letter goes inside

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
to confer is to discuss together, as at a powwow

explanation.surface: A tribal chief holds a council meeting gathered around a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A conifer is a cone-bearing tree such as a pine or fir, so it is one kind of tree.

clue.text: Here's why, we hear, it shouldn't be believed

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the noun: a belief that goes against orthodoxy

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the words are judged by their sound rather than their spelling

blocks.note: the phrase spoken quickly matches a single word

explanation.surface: Someone explains the reason a story ought not to be trusted.
explanation.definitionFit: Heresy is a belief contrary to accepted doctrine, so in the church's eyes it is something one must not believe.

clue.text: Beautiful child trapped in crèche? Rubbish

indicators.note: something trapped in the words is enclosed within them, spanning the gap between two

blocks.note: the last letters of the first word run into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A sweet-faced infant stuck in a nursery, dismissed with a cry of nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: The accent on the e is ignored, and the question mark is just punctuation to step over.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is an angel pictured as a chubby, pretty child, and by extension any lovely little child.

clue.text: What in tarnation is odd for school?

indicators.note: odd means the letters in the odd-numbered positions, first, third, fifth and so on

blocks.note: letters one, three, five, seven and nine

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry of what in tarnation, asking why a school is so strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What in tarnation' is an old American exclamation of surprise; 'school' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to teach or drill them, the same as to train them.

clue.text: Something used in cutting mediocre journalist understood

blocks.note: a hack is a writer of dull, routine journalism
I saw means I understood

explanation.surface: A second-rate reporter grasps the purpose of a cutting tool.
explanation.walkthrough: Cuttings are also newspaper clippings, which fits the journalist in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a fine-toothed saw for cutting metal, a tool used in cutting.

clue.text: Statement of aims about encore

blocks.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
an encore is a performance done again

explanation.surface: A mission statement that concerns repeating a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a set of beliefs or principles that guide one's actions, a statement of what one aims for.

clue.text: What can make a wet mixture? Right

definitions.text: What can make a wet mixture? Right

indicators.note: a mixture is things stirred together, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A cook asks what turns dry ingredients into a wet mix, and answers their own question.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer: add it to dry ingredients and you get a wet mixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Water is the liquid you add to make any mix wet, so it is what makes a wet mixture.

clue.text: Strengthening control for hard stuff

blocks.note: a rein is a strap used to control a horse, and figuratively any check
taken as written
cement is a building material that sets hard

explanation.surface: Someone argues that controlling access to strong spirits makes things more robust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard stuff' suggests strong liquor, but here it is a building material.
explanation.definitionFit: Reinforcement is the act of making something stronger, which is strengthening.

clue.text: Introvert, individual splitting left and right

indicators.note: something splitting a pair comes between them, so it goes inside

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
one means a single individual
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A shy person who stands apart, dividing the political left and right.
explanation.definitionFit: A loner prefers their own company, which describes an introvert, the opposite of a sociable person.

clue.text: Computer program for casual reader

blocks.note: first meaning: software for viewing web pages
second meaning: someone who leafs idly through books in a shop or library

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests software built for light reading; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the web-viewing software and a person who looks through things without buying or studying them.
